landing.title: HackFire: reach every resident before the fire does

hero.title: Reach every resident before the fire does
hero.lead: A voice agent calls the residents in a wildfire's predicted path, tells each one how to get out and asks whether they can leave on their own. The emergency coordinator sees on a map who is evacuating, who is not answering and who needs rescue.
hero.event: Built at HackBarna 2026 for the Norrsken and Deepfire “AI for Wildfire” challenge, track 4: values at risk.

leadTime.label: of lead time for {zone}
leadTime.start: Flagged in the fire's predicted path
leadTime.body: With only the satellite hotspots seen up to {flagged} on 23 July 2026, HackFire put {zone} in the fire's predicted path. The first hotspot within {radius} km of the estate came at {reached}.
leadTime.caveat: Computed from satellite data only. It says nothing about when the authorities warned anyone.

problem.title: The fire we replay
problem.body: On 23 July 2026 the Burgohondo wildfire in Ávila ran 3 km in 40 minutes and reached the La Atalaya housing estate in El Tiemblo. Between 1,200 and 1,300 people were evacuated from it and 5 homes were destroyed.
problem.gap: Public alerts are one-way. ES-Alert sends the same message to a whole area and does not listen: the coordinator does not know who has left, who never got the message and who cannot move.

how.title: How it works
how.lead: One day of the real fire, in twenty seconds.
how.fireTitle: The fire and where it is heading
how.fireBody: Deepfire's satellite hotspots, fresh in yellow, older in red, and a predicted spread projected from the speed and heading of the front.
how.zonesBody: The prediction is crossed with towns, housing estates, care homes and schools from OpenStreetMap. Each place gets a time to impact.
how.callTitle: A call to every resident at risk
how.callBody: The voice agent gives each resident a way out that avoids the fire and asks whether they can leave on their own.
how.triageBody: Each answer becomes a state on the map. Evacuees get their route to a safe point; each rescue goes to the fire crew with the way to the door.
how.honest: Illustrative animation: real satellite hotspots from 23 July; example residents and call.
how.map: Animated map of the fire of 23 July 2026 near El Tiemblo, Ávila.
how.call: Example call to a resident of La Atalaya
how.waiting: The calls start once a zone is in the predicted path.
how.agentLine: I'm calling from the emergency coordination about the fire. You need to leave now for San Martín de Valdeiglesias.
how.agentAsk: Can you leave on your own?
how.quote: Every resident who evacuates on their own is a rescue the firefighters don't have to make.
how.network: Calls start from the prediction, hours ahead, while the cell towers still work. No answer is a signal too: it tells the coordinator where to send a patrol.

outcomes.title: The three outcomes of a call
outcomes.evacuating: Leaving on their own, with a route to a safe point that avoids the fire.
outcomes.no_answer: Nobody picked up. The agent calls again, and the coordinator knows where to send a patrol.
outcomes.needs_rescue: Cannot leave alone. Ranked by time to impact and sent to the fire crew with the route to the door.

stack.title: What it is built on
stack.deepfireBody: Satellite hotspots for the replay, and the fires burning right now for live mode.
stack.spreadBody: A cone from the front's velocity, estimated from the last three hours of hotspots, using only what had been observed at each moment.
stack.routingBody: Routes by car and on foot that avoid the predicted fire. The fire crew's route avoids only what has already burned.
stack.voiceBody: Two voice agents, both thinking with NVIDIA Nemotron Super 3: one talks to residents, the other answers the coordinator.
stack.placesBody: Towns, housing estates, care homes, schools, health centres and roads in the fire's path.

note.title: A note on the real fire
note.body: The demo replays a real event from July 2026 in which people lost their homes. Our one headline figure, lead time, is computed from satellite data only: the gap between the moment the system flags a zone as at risk and the moment hotspots reach it. We make no claim about what the emergency services did or when.
